name: SlideRize
custom_html:
Paste a sketch's code in the panel on the right to display it here.
Sliderized!
Paste code to make sliders appear here.

---(SLIDERIZE)---P5 SKETCHES!

1/ Sketch

2/ Paste url to fetch title

Uses OpenProcessing's public oEmbed API (title only, not the code).

3/ Paste source code here


          
        

      

      

        
        
      

      
Copies this code with the current slider values baked in — paste it as sketch.js of a NEW p5.js sketch on openprocessing.org. (OpenProcessing provides its own page and its own p5.js — SlideR's own interface can't be pasted there, only the sketch you pasted into it.)

      
No code yet.

    


    

      
4/ Additional files if necessary

      

      
      
For sketches that load a shader (.glsl/.vert/.frag), a .json, or a .csv via loadShader/loadJSON/etc. Enter the exact file name used in the code and paste its content. Also works if the code instead references the file name (minus extension) as a plain JS variable it never declares (e.g. new p5.Shader(this.renderer, vert, frag) with files named vert/frag) — it gets auto-injected as a global variable too. A file whose content starts with a JS declaration (function/class/const/let/var, optional header comments first) is instead executed as its own script before your main code — for sketches split across several files (shared helper functions/classes) with no direct link to a filename. Text only — no images or sounds. Editing a file here does NOT restart the preview automatically (Restart will light up when you do) — fill in both the name and the content first, since a restart before both are ready would make a real loadShader/loadJSON genuinely fail to find the file.

    


    

      
5/ Export video (option)

      

        
        
      

      
Records the live preview. Downloads as .mp4 or .webm depending on what your browser supports.

    


    

      
6/ Image

      

        
      

      
Downloads a PNG snapshot of the current frame, with the floating "Sliderized!" panel composited on top exactly as shown on screen.

      
Also arms a hidden canvas directly on this page (not inside the preview iframe). If you're running SlideR itself as an OpenProcessing sketch: click this first, THEN click OP's own "Capture Image" — it needs a canvas directly on the page to find, which the sandboxed preview iframe normally hides from it.
